scope: Read every row of all seven archived CAPCO releases, the two code-alias attachments and the published codebook. Do not select source checks by portfolio holdings, fitted values or returns.
extraction: Extract eight original PDF cells with source page and table row. Normalize whitespace only, retaining the original cell text. Reject ambiguous grids, unreadable glyphs, duplicate security codes and unknown non-header rows.
Independently match every full row against pypdf text in source order and reconcile every six-digit source code; compare category codes, labels and parent relationships with the archived codebook.

Read section, manufacturing subclass and division levels from DOCX paragraphs while preserving table/row provenance. A merged row can also contain group-level material; published stock tables do not supply group-level assignments.
Review layout boundary examples and every extraction conflict visually; save failures without overwriting them. A visual sample is not described as complete visual certification.
Read all alias rows with old/new codes and names. Identity mapping is distinct from historical code availability, listing status and universe membership.
availability: Keep statistical period, catalogue date, PDF metadata, source retrieval time and any corroborating official page dates separate. Use no release as a live industry input in this phase; no date inferred from a migrated URL or document metadata certifies historical availability.
additional_sources: Archive the publicly linked CSRC 2024 standard and official publication article, and corroborating CAPCO release pages when available. Compare taxonomy definitions; never retroactively impose a later codebook or replace original classifications.
next_gate: Before model integration register separate static-taxonomy and dated-availability comparisons with explicit unknown-industry and ETF treatment across features, targets, allocation and independent account checks. Report historical-universe bias separately.

followup.reason: The first two source releases contain visibly truncated labels; the full code-alias attachment has continuation pages without repeated headers. Preserve the initial failure and review every row.
followup.label_findings: Compare all category names and parent codes to the codebook, recording each mismatch on its exact source row. Keep raw text unchanged. Complete extraction can pass while taxonomy findings remain; do not silently canonicalize source labels or treat a source-cell match as a classification certification.
followup.continuation: Only alias-table pages may inherit the first page header. Require five unmerged cells, horizontal column edges within 0.1 PDF point of the actual header, contiguous ordinals across every page, full independent text and code-inventory agreement, and one-to-one old/new codes. No historical trading or code-effective date is inferred from the listing-date column.
followup.verification: Freeze both the failed reader commit and prior output. Test shortened labels and shifted/missing continuation columns; rerun every registered source to a new output. No model inputs, adoption or risk rules change.
